words.gloss: to those who do not let go

literal: Clinging, do not leave, sufferings, attachment, clinging, to those who do not let go.
translation: Sufferings will cling to and never leave those who do not let go of their attachments.
modern: பற்றுகளைப் பற்றிக்கொண்டு அவற்றை விடாதவர்களை, துன்பங்கள் பற்றிக்கொண்டு விடவே மாட்டா.
explanation: This couplet highlights the inescapable cycle of desire and suffering. The poet uses the word 'பற்று' (grasp or attachment) in a dual sense: the mental grip we hold on worldly desires, and the grip that misery holds on us. Sufferings are personified as relentless forces that actively cling to and refuse to release those who refuse to let go of their own attachments. The only way to be freed from the grip of sorrow is to first release our own grasp on worldly things.
